speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected; a normal MRI makes Multiple Sclerosis less likely given your symptoms. Can you tell me exactly where on your right arm you feel the numbness, and does the weakness improve or worsen with movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of weakness, weight loss, and your history of diabetes and anabolic steroid use is highly concerning for a malignancy or severe metabolic issue rather than Multiple Sclerosis. Do you have any night sweats, fevers, or lymph node swelling? REQUEST TEST: CT Chest and Abdomen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Chest: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor; CT_Abdomen: Normal findings.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor)
